source.title: Loss-to-Loss Prediction: Scaling Laws for All Datasets
source.authors: David Brandfonbrener; Nikhil Anand; Nikhil Vyas; Eran Malach; S. Kakade

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study empirically tests power-law loss prediction and extrapolation with a different, shifted loss-to-loss method, across training datasets and downstream evaluations.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own model sweeps, loss-to-loss fits, large-run extrapolations, compute-optimal scaling exponents, and downstream loss and accuracy evaluations. Cited findings from other work are not recorded as results. The paper's main scaling-law fits use training loss; its cross-dataset and downstream analyses use evaluated losses. Individual pairwise coefficients in the flattened Table 7 are not assigned to specific pairs.
record.test_reason: The study trains 528 OLMo models (20M–1.7B, 2e17–4.84e19 FLOPs) on six datasets. It fits Chinchilla-style scaling laws per dataset and reports compute-optimal exponents (Tables 3–4). It extrapolates FLOPs-to-loss and scaling-law fits from 8 small runs to 3.3B/1e21-FLOP runs (Table 2) and relates downstream loss and error to pretraining loss. These results bear on V1, V2, V3, V6 and V7 with a different, loss-to-loss framing. It is not an original source.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The record should add that loss-to-loss translation from 8 runs nearly matches a full 88-run scaling-law fit. It should also add that, under the translation, compute-optimal model size is invariant across data distributions, which roughly holds on the six datasets.
record.recipe_differences: The paper develops shifted loss-to-loss prediction between models or evaluation distributions rather than directly reproducing the original single-distribution scaling-law fitting procedures.
record.method_sensitivity: The loss-to-loss exponent and curvature vary with dataset pair and downstream target. Test-to-test fits are noisier on some tasks. The paper compares Equation (4) with Equation (1); it does not vary pretraining hyperparameters, and explicitly flags that robustness as untested.

fits_no_version.finding: Shifted power laws relate losses across datasets and from pretraining to downstream or validation loss. These loss-to-loss fits extrapolate to 20x compute and show dataset- and task-dependent curvature.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Losses of models trained on different data, or evaluated on different distributions, are related by shifted power laws that extrapolate across scale.

fits_no_version.finding: The relation between downstream CE loss and classification error is roughly shared across pretraining datasets.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Downstream CE loss mediates the effect of pretraining data on downstream accuracy.

record.problems: The authors identify difficult estimates of asymptotic entropy, noisier train-to-test and test-to-test fits (especially at high losses), a relatively small set of downstream tasks, use of multiple-choice tasks rather than generative tasks, and untested robustness to sequence length, batch size, and learning rate. No uncertainty intervals or error bars are reported for the listed prediction errors.
record.rows_left_out: Individual curve values for the many dataset-pair and test-to-test combinations in Figures 2, 3, 5, and Appendices B-C are not separately extracted where the text provides only plots; Table 7's flattened entries do not reliably associate every coefficient with a dataset pair. The 20 Table 2 method-by-task values are represented for both proposed methods and the FLOPs, scaling-law, and identity comparators only where retained above; the independent-scaling-law comparator values are not separately retained.

untested.parts: Fits use training loss rather than a separate held-out set (single-pass, so probably equivalent, but not stated). Range is about 2 orders of magnitude in N and compute. No pure N-only or D-only power law is fit.

Extrapolation is only 20x compute (about 1.3 orders of magnitude), and only for downstream losses fit from 8 runs. There is no reported error for single-dataset scaling laws predicting the 3.3B pretraining loss.
The token-count exponent is only implied (1−a under C=6ND), not reported directly.
Depth and width are not varied at fixed parameter count.
No other modalities, repeated data, fine-tuning or transfer training. Only zero-shot evaluation on other distributions.
Generative tasks are not tested; only 11 multiple-choice tasks.
Training schedule, hyperparameters and parameter counting are not varied.

missing.what: Goodness of fit of the per-dataset Eq. (4) scaling laws: skyline R² 0.987–0.992 on 88 models per dataset.
Independent scaling laws fit from only 8 runs fit poorly: R² 0.450 on StarCoder and 0.928–0.975 elsewhere. Fit quality depends on the number of runs.
Per-dataset loss exponents: α 0.40–0.45 and β 0.43–0.47 (Eq. 4); α 0.43–0.55 and β 0.42–0.45 (Eq. 1). These show data- and parameterization-dependence of the exponents themselves.

record.verdict_notes: Table 2 rows for the study's own loss-to-loss methods were unlinked from V2, because they take the large P0 run's loss as input. V2 verdicts rest on the FLOPs-to-loss and independent-scaling-law comparators, which are genuine small-to-large power-law extrapolations of downstream loss, though only at 20x. The general train-to-test rows stay on V6 because they predict downstream loss from pretraining loss. The V1 verdict comes from the text (Table 1) with no row, and the fits use training loss, likely single-pass.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not directly test held-out pretraining cross-entropy as a power law in parameters, tokens, and compute with the other quantities not bottlenecking; its Appendix D scaling-law fits use training loss.
The study tests extrapolation of shifted loss-to-loss fits to larger runs, not whether the original single-dataset scaling laws alone predict larger runs.

The study reports the fitted compute exponent for optimal model size and derives invariance across datasets under its translation, but does not directly measure the token-count exponent for the compute-optimal allocation.
Depth, width, and other architecture details are not varied at fixed parameter count.
The study covers text pretraining datasets and zero-shot downstream tasks, not other modalities, repeated-data training, fine-tuning, or transfer-training regimes.
Downstream loss and classification error are evaluated; the paper does not test every downstream task or generative-task performance.

The study observes dataset- and target-dependent loss-to-loss exponents and compares two scaling-law parameterizations, but does not vary the stated training hyperparameters or systematically establish why published studies disagree.

rows.subject: OLMo models trained on the six pre-training datasets
rows.operation_detail: Fit shifted power laws relating training losses of models paired on parameter count and training tokens across different datasets.

conditions.value: FineWeb, FineWeb-Edu, Proof Pile 2, SlimPajama, SmolLM Corpus, StarCoder v1
fits use 2e17 to 4.84e19 FLOPs; extrapolation runs use 1e21 FLOPs
same parameter count N and training tokens D

rows.measure: Shifted power-law relationship between paired training losses
rows.value: The text reports κ ranging from 0.88 to 1.13 across dataset pairs; K ranges as far as 0.55 or 1.72 between SmolLM Corpus and ProofPile, depending on prediction direction.
rows.locator: Section 4.1; Figure 2; discussion of parameter values
rows.note: The text says the shifted power law fits the relationships and that κ varies by dataset pair; exact per-pair coefficients from Table 7 are not assigned because its flattened layout is ambiguous.
rows.check: This is the fit itself, not an extrapolation, so drop V2. κ≠1 implies dataset-dependent loss exponents (α1=κα0), which bears on V7. The text says κ min 0.88 and max 1.13 occur between StarCoder and SlimPajama.

source_check.locator_found: Section 4.1, Figure 2 and Parameter values paragraph: κ ranges from 0.88 to 1.13; K extremes are 0.55 and 1.72.

rows.subject: OLMo models trained on FineWeb and evaluated on pre-training validation distributions
rows.operation_detail: Fit shifted power-law relationships from training loss to validation loss on other pre-training distributions.
rows.measure: Validation cross-entropy loss versus source training loss
rows.value: The paper describes the relationship as convex, with diminishing transfer returns as FineWeb loss falls.
rows.note: The authors say the pattern occurs for sources with little or no code evaluated on the all-code StarCoder distribution.
rows.check: Curvature of a train-loss to validation-loss relation is a loss-to-loss shape, not a scaling exponent or a fitting choice. Not V7.

rows.subject: OLMo models trained on the six pre-training datasets
rows.operation_detail: Fit shifted power-law relationships from training loss to validation loss across pre-training distributions.
rows.measure: Curvature of training-loss to validation-loss relationships
rows.value: Many curves are close to linear, while the FineWeb-to-code example is convex.
rows.note: The authors also report that asymptotic transfer losses can remain substantially worse than training directly on the target distribution.
rows.check: Same as r3: a loss-to-loss curvature result, not a V7 measure.

rows.subject: OLMo models trained on the six pre-training datasets
rows.operation_detail: Fit shifted power laws from pretraining loss to downstream-task cross-entropy loss.

conditions.value: cross-entropy loss of the correct multiple-choice answer phrased as a cloze task

rows.measure: Downstream loss as a function of pretraining training loss
rows.value: The paper reports smooth shifted-power-law relationships, with more curvature than for pre-training validation distributions; downstream-task relationships are typically concave (κ < 1).
rows.note: The paper describes concave relationships as increasing returns to reductions in training loss.
rows.check: Downstream loss is smooth in pretraining loss, which bears on V6. Curvature is not V7, so drop V7.

rows.subject: OLMo models trained on the six pre-training datasets
rows.operation_detail: Fit shifted power laws from training loss to downstream validation loss.
rows.measure: Curvature of the training-loss to downstream-loss relationship
rows.value: Some tasks are convex (κ > 1) and others concave (κ < 1); downstream tasks are typically concave.
rows.note: The study reports target-task-dependent curve shapes rather than one universal exponent.
rows.check: Convex vs concave loss-to-loss shape is a different construct from V6 predictability or V7 fit-dependence.

rows.subject: OLMo models trained on FineWeb-Edu and five other pre-training datasets
rows.operation_detail: Fit test-to-test shifted power laws and evaluate them on larger models.
rows.measure: Prediction of downstream test loss across training datasets
rows.value: The paper says the fits generally extrapolate to models trained with 20x the FLOP budget of the largest model used to fit them; Hellaswag fits are especially good and other downstream tasks are noisier.
rows.note: The authors attribute the greater noise on some downstream tasks to evaluation noise affecting both axes.
rows.check: Test-to-test loss-to-loss extrapolation is the study's own method and uses the large P0 run as input. Not a scale extrapolation.

conditions.value: seven OLMo tasks and their aggregate

rows.measure: Downstream classification error predicted from pretraining loss
rows.value: The aggregate fit is described as fairly good, but some individual fits, including Hellaswag and ARC-Challenge, are described as systematically wrong.
rows.note: The authors explain that the unconstrained power-law form can predict errors beyond the possible chance-error range.
